source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: From the ascendant to the mid-heaven, or from the angle of the west to the lower heaven, they are considered to be masculine, being then oriental: and in the other two quadrants, feminine, being then occidental.

normalized_rule: Classify positions from the Ascendant to the mid-heaven and from the western angle to the lower heaven as oriental, and positions in the other two horizon quadrants as occidental.
synthesis_notes: This is a Ptolemaic horizon-quadrant classification, not a generic later definition of oriental/occidental.
review_notes: Retained ID is now limited to the horizon-quadrant statement; the separate matutine/vespertine rule carries the Sun-relative classification.
transmission_notes: The rule follows the horizon-quadrant wording in the Ashmand/Proclus passage and must remain distinct from the Sun-relative matutine/vespertine statement. Certainty is scoped to this cited transmission.
